purpose: Reference design examples. Scalar cases are executable by package validator; scenario cases require production C# owner/UI tests and are not executed here.

cases.case: Models: local adds provider/model X preferred; remote adds Y preferred
cases.expected_behavior: Group conflict: retain at most one preferred model, without inventing a requirement to choose one; retain both rows unless the user removes one.

cases.case: Base row id=42; local deletes; remote edits its address
cases.expected_behavior: Delete/edit conflict; never match another row at the old array index.
Merged membership={b,c,d}; no resurrection of a.

cases.case: Raw numeric input="-" while typed value is still 0.5; remote changes title
cases.expected_behavior: Keep invalid raw input and validation; merge title without substituting parsed 0.5 for raw draft.

cases.case: Base B; submitted S; local edited after dispatch; accepted A; current read is already R2
cases.expected_behavior: A establishes own accepted baseline; later edits retained; R2 is foreign/current read, not own receipt.

cases.case: Foreign archive then local content merge
cases.expected_behavior: No implicit restore; current lifecycle must be explicitly handled.

cases.case: Merge applies M over R, then local undo restores pre-merge L
cases.expected_behavior: Expected remote authority stays R; dirty recomputed, no return to old B token.

cases.case: Third writer commits after R read but before subsequent Save
cases.expected_behavior: Owner refuses stale expectation; preserve M and re-open review without force retry.

cases.case: A newer coherent baseline R2 was already legitimately adopted; the delayed acknowledgement A for an older submission arrives later
cases.expected_behavior: Attach the exact historical accepted outcome without rolling the current baseline, native expectation, draft or view back to A. A current read alone must not be treated as proof of that old operation.
